rationale: B wins because it keeps the angles inside the facts and treats the holes as holes, not confetti. Its best line, "Without that person this angle does not exist — do not pitch it on the feature alone," is exactly the discipline this update needs. A has real bones, but "Discord Needs a Revenue Story Before It Can IPO" is built partly on the invented claim that this is Discord's "first real monetization product," and the set keeps smuggling in Patreon, Twitch, YouTube, and Substack before the facts earn them.
gaps_in_A: "first real monetization product" is invented. The update says Discord is launching paid creator subscriptions, not that Discord has no existing revenue products.
"Millions of Unpaid Gaming Community Managers Just Got a Business Model" overstates the supplied facts. The update gives 200M MAU, not millions of server owners, unpaid managers, or adoption intent.
"in range with Patreon and Twitch" and later "alongside Patreon, Substack, and YouTube memberships" import competitor framing not supplied by the update.
"the company explicitly compares this to the 30% app-store standard" is too confident. The facts say the fee is below the standard, not that Discord made that comparison as positioning.
gaps_in_B: "active, ongoing argument" around app-store fee fights is a light external peg, not supplied in the update, though it is at least used as beat context rather than a fake fact.
"right before an IPO" is a little hot. The update says reportedly preparing for an IPO, not that timing is imminent.
"run a large gaming community for free" is plausible color but not in the supplied facts; B wisely makes the named server owner proof non-negotiable, but the line still leans past the record.
